title: MACOCHA Score — Difficult Intubation in the ICU
keywords: score 3 or more predicts difficult intubation
sources: De Jong A, Molinari N, Terzi N, et al. Early identification of patients at risk for difficult intubation in the intensive care unit: development and validation of the MACOCHA score. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2013;187:832-839
De Jong A, et al. Difficult intubation in the ICU — external validation and refinement. Intensive Care Med 2018

changelog.change: Initial entry — the ICU-specific difficult-intubation predictor (7 factors, 0-12), converted from the CV Difficult Airway guide.

purpose: Predicts difficult tracheal intubation in critically ill patients before induction. Built and validated in the ICU population (not the OR), where difficult intubation carries a far higher rate of severe hypoxaemia and cardiac arrest. Use it to decide, before you push the drugs, whether to bring the most experienced operator, a double set-up, or an awake technique.

items.label: Reduced mobility of the cervical spine

interpretation.label: Lower predicted risk of difficult intubation
interpretation.detail: Below the validated threshold. Still run a pre-intubation team brief, optimise positioning and pre-oxygenation, and keep a bougie and a supraglottic rescue at the bedside — 29% of ICU difficult airways in the ID-ACCT cohort were not identifiable in advance.

interpretation.label: Difficult intubation predicted (score ≥ 3)
interpretation.detail: At/above the derivation threshold (sensitivity ~73%, specificity ~89%). Most experienced operator on the first attempt, video laryngoscopy first-line, bougie/stylet loaded, second-generation SGA and a cricothyrotomy kit physically present. Verbalise the plan A→B→C→D out loud before induction. If CICO risk is also high, consider an awake technique.

interpretation.label: High predicted risk of difficult intubation
interpretation.detail: Treat as an anticipated difficult airway. Double set-up (surgical airway marked and prepped), airway expert / ENT or surgery on standby or in the room, awake flexible-scope or awake video-laryngoscopy intubation if oxygenation and cooperation allow. Do not proceed with a single-operator asleep attempt.

notes: MACOCHA components spell the mnemonic: Mallampati III/IV, Apnoea (OSA), Cervical spine mobility reduced, Opening of mouth < 3 cm, Coma, Hypoxaemia, Anaesthesiologist absent. The first three factors are patient-related, the next two pathology-related, the last two operator/context-related. A score ≥ 3 was the derivation cut-off; risk rises continuously with the score, so 6+ is meaningfully worse than 3. Related: LEMON airway assessment, The Difficult Airway (DAS 2025), The Physiologically Difficult Airway, Airway Management Flow.
buildNote: Additive engine, straightforward. Bands: <3 low, 3-5 and 6-12 both 'high' severity but with escalating action text (there is no separate published 'moderate' band — ≥3 is the single validated threshold).
